### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/ui/react-pages.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx`  _(via os explain (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `75650b1cc72e32c21e776c29a9610d2f4c247f92` — the merge of head `545f84ccce8d825e263e26f1af330147b0c08aae` into base `78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 75650b1cc72e32c21e776c29a9610d2f4c247f92 && git checkout 75650b1cc72e32c21e776c29a9610d2f4c247f92
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0 545f84ccce8d825e263e26f1af330147b0c08aae && git checkout -B drift-repro 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0 && git merge --no-ff 545f84ccce8d825e263e26f1af330147b0c08aae

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 78f7160e0fbef5ef7e015f6a90d97ff0e069cbb0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #35985: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #36089: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `788cf6680e7e3c2af660688c9d8c1c183ad42929`
  · the check-runs on `788cf6680e7e3c2af660688c9d8c1c183ad42929`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

Security — a `hits` path sits on the low-risk skills arm: when the change teaches security, auth or permission
  behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label.
  The record says so on its `Security-touching:` line, and the arm lands on `no` alone: write `no` ONLY when no changed
  hunk teaches permission, sharing, credential, token, authentication or other security behaviour, else `yes`.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/3d3cbaf6-4903-5fed-92d4-c2b94a45e868/scratchpad/pr-36089/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `788cf6680e7e3c2af660688c9d8c1c183ad42929`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md + none

Read for this record: card #35985 (body and its four comments), PR #36089 (body, file list, comments), the net diff `33d01694..788cf668` (3 files, +14 −4), and the check-runs on the head. The diff holds no gate, validator or code, so nothing in it implements the two `hits` files; `.changeset/35985-object-color-skills.md` is the lane seat's remainder. The code the sentences describe was read on `main` 33d01694 and is not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged, and described right.** The diff changes no schema. The nine names in the new `color` row are `OBJECT_COLORS` in `packages/spec/src/data/object-icon.ts`, same names, same order (`gray blue teal green amber orange red pink purple`). "(no hex)" is right: `OBJECT_COLOR_SCHEMA` is `z.enum(OBJECT_COLORS).optional()`, so any other string is refused. `ObjectSchema.color` reads that leaf (`object.zod.ts:3936`), so `"color": "blue"` in the example parses.
- **Default `gray`: right as drawn, not as stored.** The schema has no `.default`; an object with no `color` stores nothing and `objectColorOrDefault` in `ui/packages/components/src/custom/object-icon-tile.tsx` draws `gray`. The spec's own `.describe` says "Omit to draw the neutral `gray`", so the table's Default cell matches the published wording.
- **Public surface: none.** No export, no type, no CLI output. `os explain object` is not in this diff (see ③).
- **Skill gates: green on the head.** `Type Check · source gates` (the skills token ratchet, skill links, frame sync and frame freshness) and `Lint · docs & code guards` (skill identifier liveness) concluded success, as did the other Lint and Type Check lanes, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. The PR body's ratchet figures (6703 / 6710 and 2563 / 2564) were not re-run; the check-run is the verdict. `Test Core (1/10)` and `(2/10)` were still running at 13:39Z; they exercise no file in this diff, and the merge gate waits for them as usual.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` patch is right: two published skill files change wording, nothing else ships. `Clause-②: no` on the PR body and in the changeset is right: no export and no schema. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Security-touching: no`, with one line the adopting seat should see.** The first SKILL.md hunk rewraps the object example, so its added line carries `"sharingModel": "public_read_write"`. The key and value are byte-identical to the removed line; only `"color": "blue"` is new. The second navigation.md hunk sits under a bullet that says "Never treat it as security", which is context and unchanged. No hunk adds, removes or rewords permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication teaching. If the seat reads "changed hunk" as any hunk whose added line names a sharing key, the line is `yes` and the PR stays Tier H.
- **PR title names a change the diff does not hold.** The title ends "os explain object lists it"; the head has no `packages/cli` file. The PR's docs-drift comment (13:07Z, `@objectstack/cli`, `explain.ts`) is from an earlier head. A squash would put that subject on `main`. Fix the title before merge (it does not move the head). Listed as N2 below.
- **`Fixes #35985` closes the card with two ends open and no card number for either. Escalated to the seat.** The claim amendment (7063042977) put `packages/cli/src/commands/explain.ts` and a `@objectstack/cli` changeset in this PR's file surface; the PR drops both and says the seat files a card. The card's acceptance line "让 AI 新建一个三个对象的应用：三个对象各有颜色，互不相同" is not met in this repository: the PR body says the blueprint-to-object step lives in the AI service, and that "the seat files that card". Neither follow-up is named by number on the card or the PR. Before the merge closes #35985, the seat either links both follow-up cards on #35985 or changes `Fixes` to `Part of`. The claim (7057663302) already ruled the AI passthrough "not a blocker for this card", so this is tracking, not a review finding.
- **PR 2 L2 N1** (a coloured object with no `icon` draws no tile on four hosts): carried in the PR body, unchanged. The skill text asks for `icon` on every object, and the new row says the console draws `icon` on the tile, so the text does not promise a tile for an icon-less object.
- **SQL push-down:** nothing to check, the diff holds no code.
- `open_questions`: none on the card or the PR.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`** — against card item 6 ("新建对象时给一个颜色，同一个应用里的对象尽量不重复；技能文档里写明可用的颜色名") and the spec on `main`.

- The row gives the names, the refusal of anything else, the default, what the colour is for, and the two authoring rules, in the table an author reads when writing an object. The first example an agent copies now carries `color` beside `icon`. That is what the card asks of the skill text.
- "the console draws `icon` white on it" holds: `ObjectIconTile` is `text-white` on `OBJECT_COLOR_TILE_CLASS[name]`.
- Tried to break "avoid repeats in one app": the palette has nine names, eight besides the neutral, so an app with ten objects must repeat. "avoid" is soft and does not instruct the impossible. It matches the card's "尽量不重复".
- Tried to break "Give every object one": `gray` is a palette name, so an agent can satisfy the rule with `gray` on every object and the card's "three objects, three colours" line still holds only through "avoid repeats". Both halves are in the row, so the row is sufficient.
- N1 (nit) — the Quick-Start Template the skill links as "one complete object" (`skills/objectstack-data/references/examples-objects.md`, `support_case`) carries `icon` and no `color`, so the skill's fullest example does not follow the new "Give every object one". An object with no colour is valid and draws gray, so nothing breaks. Follow-up card, or leave.

**`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md`** — against `ui/packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx` and `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/nav-menu-renderer.tsx` on `main`.

- "An `object` item's icon sits on its object's `color` tile." holds in both renderers: an item with `type: 'object'` and an `objectName` draws `ObjectIconTile`, the glyph from `resolveNavItemIcon` (the item's own `icon`, else the object's), the colour from the object alone (`resolveTargetColor` / `targetColor`); every other item type draws the line icon. The sentence sits right after the keys-by-type list that says `icon` is on every item, which is where an author would otherwise expect an item-level colour. It names no key the item accepts, so it invites no `color` on a navigation item.
- The two trims lose nothing an author needs. "The nav item's shape selects the mode:" sits under the heading "Three Run Modes: Object Nav vs Filters Slice vs Interface Pages", which carries the dropped subject. "(or one-off view)" for "(or a view authored for a one-off slice)" is still carried by the `filters` bullet above it ("Don't author a view for it") and the one-sentence rule below it.
- N2 (nit) — the PR title's "os explain object lists it" is not true of the head (see ③). Prose; fix in the title.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The merge adds nothing to the PR's files.** The three blobs are identical at both heads: `.changeset/35985-object-color-skills.md` `3ceb5f4a`, `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` `d892c6eb`, `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md` `c9f8c814`. `main` did not touch either skill file between the two merge bases (`5459b826` and `22ecb750` at both).

The merge base is the merged `main` tip, so the head's whole tree differs from `main` in these three files only; the merge commit carries no change of its own.
- **Accept set and public surface: unchanged.** `ObjectSchema.color` still reads `OBJECT_COLOR_SCHEMA` (`object.zod.ts:3936`); `packages/spec/src/data/object-icon.ts` did not move on `main`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Security-touching: no`, same reading as before.** No new text entered the PR's files. The one line worth naming is unchanged: the rewrapped example line carries `"sharingModel": "public_read_write"`, byte-identical to the line it replaces.

- SQL push-down: nothing to check, the diff holds no code.
